title: Captures on board A load the mating attack on board B
summary: Both boards swung back and forth, with a promoted queen for each side on board B and pieces crossing in both directions. Near the end White on board A gave up a rook and fell behind there, but its captures sent Black on board B a bishop, a rook, a pawn and a queen, which Black dropped one after another to mate. Follow the bishop from Ba6+: it crosses to board A, captures there, and comes back as B@f3+.
event: HypeBeast 1.1.1 (pre-release build) against HypeBeast 1.1.0, 500,000 nodes a move

result.text: Black on board B mates; the team of A-White and B-Black wins.

moves.note: Its first choice was exd5. It dropped a pawn on g4 instead, preferring it in case a knight came from board A, and none came. That pawn went on to take the knight on f3 with gxf3, then the pawn on g2, and promoted with gxh1=Q, taking the rook. The knight and the rook went to White on board A, who dropped them later as N@e5 and R@h8.

Its first choice was Bxh2+, but it took the knight on d5 instead, because that capture sends a knight to its partner, White on board B, where by its count one more knight was worth about three and a half pawns. White on board B dropped that knight as N@h4 a few moves later.

lines.note: White's answer, P@h6 and then hxg7, both played in the game.
Its first choice: after Bxh2+ Nxh2, Bxd1 takes White's queen.
A search that ignores the other board drops a knight on this board with N@h4, which scored about a pawn and a half better for Black than exd5 searched the same way.

moves.note: The knight Black took on d5 with exd5 on board A arrives here. Its first choice was Be3; it preferred N@h4 because it thought a pawn trade on board A about as likely as not, and in that case it scored N@h4 much better. Pawns were traded there, hxg7 and then Rxg7. The knight stayed on h4 until Black took it with Rxh4, sending it to White on board A.

The queen Black made with gxh1=Q takes the bishop on f1 with check and is taken by Kxf1. The bishop goes to White on board A, who drops it as B@h6, while the promoted queen reaches Black on board A only as a pawn. Black scored itself more than five pawns up here.

White was in check from Ba6+ and blocked with P@b5, using the pawn Black's Rxg7 had just taken on board A; the engine had expected that pawn more often than not. The pawn also attacks the bishop. Black took the promoted queen on a8 with Qxa8, which reaches White on board A only as a pawn, and White took the bishop with bxa6, sending it to its partner on board A.

lines.note: The game followed this line for two moves, Qxa8 and then bxa6.

moves.note: Its first choice was N@h3+, but the engine expected a piece to come from board B before its next move, most likely a bishop, and with a bishop in hand it scored N@h3+ much worse than Rg6. The bishop came, from bxa6, and Black dropped it as B@f6 a few moves later. By its next move Black's own score had gone from about five pawns down to about half a pawn down.

lines.note: White's answer in a fresh search, N@g7+ and R@g3, still scored White well ahead.
Its first choice, N@h3+, which White takes with gxh3.

moves.note: The pawn came from board B, where Black's Qxa8 took White's promoted queen, which returns to the hand as a pawn; the engine had given that arrival a high chance. Dropped on g7 beside the rook on h8, it scored White about nine pawns up, but by White's next move here the score was about three pawns down, after bxa6 on board B sent Black a bishop. Black's own search still scored White slightly ahead, so nothing here shows why White's score fell.

lines.note: White's own line, with R@h8 after Black's Rg8.
Black's own line at its next move, with the bishop from board B in hand, still scored White a little ahead.

moves.note: The bishop that came from board B and was dropped on f6 now takes White's bishop on g5, which goes to Black's partner, White on board B, who drops it with check as B@b5+. The engine scored this about 14 pawns in Black's favour, nearly all of it for what that bishop is worth on board B, where its partner was losing; on this board alone it was about level. White's own search at its next move scored White ahead.

lines.note: Black's own line, a run of captures on both sides, each one handing a piece across.
A search that ignores the other board plays Bxg7, which scored a little better for Black than Bxg5 when both were searched the same way.
White's own line at its next move, Nxc6 and Nxd8+, which its search scored in White's favour.

moves.note: The bishop Black just took on g5 on board A arrives, and White gives check with it. Its first choice was B@a4+, but the engine expected a knight from board A more than one time in three, and with a knight in hand it scored B@b5+ far better. The knight came at once: its partner took White's knight on c6 with bxc6, and White here later dropped it as N@d5.

lines.note: Black blocks with P@c6, as in the game.
Its first choice, B@a4+, answered by P@d7.
A search that ignores the other board plays Qg3, which scored a little better than B@b5+ searched the same way, without counting the knight to come.

moves.note: This bishop has crossed the boards twice: it was Black's bishop on a6 here, went to board A after bxa6, was dropped there as B@f6, took on g5, and came back when White took it with Bxg5. Dropped with check on f3, it raised Black's score to about 18 pawns in its favour.

White gives up the rook for the pawn on e4, since Black recaptures with dxe4. By its count each piece it captured would help its partner and the rook it lost would cost nothing on board B, so nearly all of its high score was for the other board. The rook went to White on board B, who never used it; the pawn went to Black on board B and became P@g2+ in the mating net. Here White's score fell to about three pawns down by its next move, once Black had received a bishop and a rook from board B.

lines.note: White's own line after dxe4, with Bxd8 among its captures, which the game also saw.
A search that ignores the other board takes the queen at once with Bxd8, which scored a little better than Rxe4+ searched the same way.
Black's own line at its next move, with the bishop from board B in hand, scored Black about seven pawns ahead after N@h3+.

moves.note: White takes Black's queen on d8. The queen goes to Black on board B, who had given that arrival about an even chance when it played R@g1+, and it is the piece that mates with Q@e1# at the end.

Black on board B was close to mating its partner, and by the engine's count one more piece of any kind was enough for Black there to mate, so every piece White captured here was very costly. Recapturing on d8 with Kxd8 or Rxd8 scored far worse than N@h3+. It also expected Black on board B to take a queen, and Nxf3+ did, sending that queen to White here; White answered Kf1 and never dropped it.

lines.note: Black's own line, in which White takes the knight with gxh3; that capture is why the engine scored the position only about even.
The line it planned for White receiving a queen; the game followed it through N@h3+ Kf1 R@h1+ Ke2.

moves.note: The pawn is the one White took on e4 with Rxe4+ on board A. By its count Black mates in three. A search that ignores the other board starts with Q@e1+ instead, also mating.

lines.note: Black's mating line: after Ke2 N@g1+, White went Kd1 instead of Ke3 and was mated by Q@e1#.
A search that ignores the other board mates with Q@e1+ first.

moves.note: Mate in two by its count. Moving the knight from f3 with Ng1+ instead scored about five pawns down for Black. The dropped knight came from board A, where White took one on c6 with Nxc6.

lines.note: The line expects Ke3 and Q@d4+; White played Kd1 instead and was mated by Q@e1#.

moves.note: Every move lost to mate in one by its count, so White sat for a second while its partner on board A, who was on move and ahead there, played. The partner's Bxf3+ sent it a pawn, but it was still mated in one by its count, and it played Kd1. Its last moves were forced, not mistakes.
The queen is the one White took on d8 with Bxd8 on board A. Dropped on e1 it is mate, and the team of White on board A and Black on board B wins.
